note: Derives: axe into bare flesh is depth 2.0 bleeding 2.0, the heavier sword bites deeper (2.96), the cuirass as a thing takes the first swing at integrity 2.4 and parts on the third, and the wound is still bleeding an hour on. Does not: a force act at a body always meets bare FLESH, so a cuirass in the world changes nothing (armoured 2.32 = naked 2.32); and 'bleeding badly' costs only 0.41 health in the hour (the worst wound on the scale, 5/5, takes over four hours to kill), which I flag as a magnitude doubt rather than a rule error because my one-fifth-in-an-hour threshold is my reading of 'bleeding badly'.

B8 impairment: a numbed arm

note: Derives: the hide face (shared leather, a sheet) holds the first knife thrust at 1.85 and parts on the second, exactly as told, and the board loses integrity with every thrust so hits absorbed are tracked. Does not: a thrust takes 0.4 off the plank (4.57, 4.15, 3.75), so it cracks after five and fails after fourteen, not three; the scenario may be generous to a skinning knife, so that is a magnitude gap, not an error. RULE ERROR in force.ts blow()/woundBody: bare hands at effort 5 leave no mark on a body (1*5*0.5+0.3 = 2.8 against flesh's 3.7), and a cudgel at ordinary effort 2 leaves none either, because a blow on a body must clear the same toughness-and-bulk bar that decides whether a thing fractures. The general rule: a body bruises in proportion to momentum from the first, and only breaking needs a threshold.

note: Derives: nothing is zeroed when the fight ends. A thigh cut of 3 is still bleeding 2.1 two hours on and has cost 1.2 health, a scratch of 0.5 has closed inside the hour, and both wounds are still there next day (health 2.6 for the rival). Does not: a coat act aimed at a body finds nothing to coat and cloth is too hard to spread, so binding is impossible; hunger does not move with time; a wound cannot fester; dizziness has nowhere to live.

needs: taste (asked for and not granted, section 8)
ingesting a coat: the film of sap and dust is what a lick takes, and ingest sees only the thing
care read by force on a body (Manner.care is ignored in woundBody)
note: Derives well at the ends: a lick at effort 0 of a cold edge does nothing and leaves the sword as it was, a swing opens 2.8, and the same lick of a blade left in the fire burns the tongue 1.3 with no cut, all from state and not from the verb. RULE ERROR 1, force.ts cut() with driven(): keenness is added to depth and effort only caps it at effort*2, so a tongue pressed at effort 1 is cut 1.52 deep, over half a full swing (2.8) and deeper than a cudgel swung with everything (0.96). The general rule: the arm drives and the edge only decides how much of that drive becomes depth, so depth should scale with effort, not start from edge minus a constant. RULE ERROR 2, body.ts ingest(): it consumes a share of any thing whatever its hardness, size or form, so the lick takes 1% of the iron and 'eat the sword' swallows it whole with no harm. The general rule: a mouth takes only what flows, is granular, or is soft enough for teeth to part, and otherwise takes nothing (or the coat). My encoding of a lick as force plus ingest is a judgment; the ingest error stands on 'eat the sword' alone.

note: Derives: bare hands at any effort do nothing to the bear, and a paw swung hard opens depth 2.3 bleeding 2.3, so the player leaves bleeding. But that is exactly what a hand axe does in a man's hand, because the bear's strength cannot be said, and a cudgel wounds the bear exactly as it wounds the man (0.96 each). Why the bear strikes, and that it stops, is choice and is unbuilt.
